html:
Dili, on the north coast of Timor, became the capital of Portuguese Timor in 1769, when the governor moved there after the Topasses drove him from Lifau.

It grew slowly as a colonial port and administrative town. Japanese bombing during the Battle of Timor in 1942 wrecked much of it, and Indonesian troops landed there in the invasion of 1975.

The Santa Cruz massacre of 1991 took place in its cemetery. Militias burned most of Dili in 1999, and it was rebuilt as the capital of the new state in 2002.
